content:
incident-bot: ALERT — p99 latency SLO breached for Elysian Payments (tenant: elysian-payments) in eu1 dedicated pool. Current p95: 340ms, p99: 1.9s. Error rate normal. Impact: payment tokenization and card verification requests slower; customer reporting timeouts. Paging oncall.

mina: oncall here — joining war room. 👋 Can someone confirm whether this is isolated to elysian tenant or affecting other tenants in the same dedicated pool? I see spike aligned with sustained qps bump for that tenant.

sophie: adding context from account team — elysian is on a reserved dedicated pool in eu1, high-volume batch jobs started 05:30 UTC. They've got scheduled settlements right now. CC @alice for customer comms.

raj: quick check of infra metrics — node-level GPU 0 utilization at 96% on pool eu1-dedicated-3, KV cache miss rate spiked ~3x at 05:32. Looks like longer decode loops, increased tail. No obvious hardware errors.

mina: ok. First mitigation plan: 1) enable tenant-level rate limit to flatten spikes 2) route new traffic for elysian to warm spare in eu2 3) evict any noisy tenants on same pool if found. Sophie / Alice can you coordinate customer notice for temporary throttling + failover? :warning:

alice: will call the AM and post a brief note to the customer Slack channel. Draft status: "We're seeing elevated request latency for some payment operations — we're applying a temporary routing change to safeguard throughput and will share ETA within 10 minutes." Any objections? :telephone_receiver:

jordan: ops note — can we do a non-disruptive routing change? Prefer `drain` then cutover. Avoid model rollback unless necessary.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline snapshot found at build/2026-03-15-2203. No outstanding canary failures. Automated healthchecks green for eu2 warm spare images.

mina: executing commands to move traffic. Running:
```
redwoodctl tenant throttle set --tenant elysian-payments --rate 200rps --window 60s
redwoodctl routes update --tenant elysian-payments --from eu1 --to eu2 --mode gradual --drain 30s
```

raj: logs show a sub-tenant (client_id: ely-prod-42) issuing long-running rerank calls every 10s during the spike. I'm pulling sample traces now.

sophie: ops-lead, do we want to isolate that sub-tenant? If it's noisy we should evict or limit it while we investigate.

ops-lead: yes, pre-approve eviction for noisy sub-tenant if it reduces p99 quickly. Use tenant-isolate playbook (link: https://internal.playbooks/tenant-isolate). Keep legal/account informed.

mina: routing change started at 05:38 UTC. Monitoring...

(40s later)

mina: quick update — p99 dropped to 820ms after throttling + partial failover, p95 back to 280ms. Still above target, but progress. Traces indicate model attention loops were the dominant CPU time for the heavy requests.

raj: initiated an immediate tenant eviction for client_id ely-prod-42 from eu1 pool; traffic rejected to force retry and smooth the queue. Command:
```
redwoodctl tenant evict --tenant ely-prod-42 --pool eu1-dedicated-3 --reason "noisy rerank jobs"
```

sophie: customer is aware and accepts temporary throttling/eviction. They're asking whether a warm standby will handle settlement window — Alice, pls confirm with them.

alice: on call with AM — elysian confirms they can tolerate short routing to eu2, prefer we keep them informed every 10m. Preparing status update for their SREs.

(3m later)

mina: p99 now at 410ms, p95 260ms. Error rates stable. Looks like eviction + routing sufficed. Shifting to containment mode. We're keeping throttles in place for 20m and monitoring KV cache warmup in eu2.

raj: follow-up: KV cache miss rate in eu2 is initially high (cold cache) — we have two options: 1) pre-populate critical prefixes from eu1 snapshot (`kv-sync --tenant elysian --target eu2`) 2) keep gradual traffic and let cache warm naturally. I recommend pre-populate to minimize tail.

mina: go ahead with pre-populate. Command queued:
```
kv-sync --tenant elysian-payments --from eu1-dedicated-3 --to eu2-warm-1 --prefixes payment/tokenization,payment/verify --parallel 4
```

deploy-bot: kv-sync job started (job id kv-87321). ETA ~120s.

mina: action checklist so far:
- throttled elysian tenant to 200rps ✅
- started gradual route to eu2 ✅
- evicted noisy sub-tenant ✅
- kicked off KV pre-populate ✅
- account team notified ✅

sophie: great. Next: we should schedule follow-up RCA to determine root cause — likely combination of bursty reranks + cold KV on failover + model variant tail. I'll own customer postmortem with @alice.

ops-lead: assign severity P1-SLO because an enterprise customer experienced breach of contract SLO. Triage notes saved to incident tracker (INC-2026-0413).

mina: handing off to morning oncall raj for post-containment monitoring and RCA. Raj, you'll own the next 2 hours and coordinate with eng-ml if traces point to model regression.

raj: taking over. I'll keep throttles until KV is stable or until 06:10 UTC, whichever comes first. If p99 creeps above 700ms I'll escalate to eng-runtime. Added runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/reduce-p99. :gear:

alice: posted customer update: "Latency spike detected; we've applied temporary routing and rate limits. Performance improving; we'll follow up with RCA within 24h." They appreciated the rapid response.

mina: final note — monitoring shows steady state for 10m, no further regressions. We'll keep incident open until RCA and follow-up mitigation (limit sched batch jobs, set tenant QPS guardrails) are completed.

ops-lead: thanks team. Keep INC-2026-0413 updated. Closing war room after handoff. :white_check_mark:

(End of thread)
